IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2b_5a: With the rope and planks we sent, the bell rang again. People came out of hiding to listen, and Pike wept in front of them all.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2b_5x: The bell never rang again. Pike took off his collar; he still looks after the people in the basement, but no longer calls himself a preacher.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_1: Dewey promised to drive six people from the Echo Creek farms out of the county in the Ark.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_2: Before the first run, the Ark needed spare tires and tools.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_3: With the tires and tools we found loaded, Dewey test-drove to the county line and back, singing the whole way.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_3x: No tires came. One blew on the test run and the Ark nearly rolled.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_4: A horde gathered across the convoy road, more than even the Ark could push through.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_5a: We cleared the horde and the convoy made it. Dewey drove six people past the county line and came back for more. They call the Ark 'the ferry' now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_5x: The horde was still there, and the Ark went into a ditch with everyone inside. Two did not get out. Dewey does not talk about the Ark.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_1: Someone stole the Ark's engine block from Dewey's garage. Vic's boys had been seen nearby.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_2: Vic said he 'found' the engine and would sell it back. It was up to us how Dewey got it back.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_3a: We went into Coalfield with Dewey and took the engine back. Vic sulked, and Dewey could not stop grinning.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_3r: We paid Vic. The engine came back, but Dewey still swears whenever it comes up.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_3g: We left it to Whitaker, and his soldiers raided Coalfield and brought the engine back. Vic was furious with everyone.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_3x: The engine never came back. Dewey sold the Ark's frame for parts and grew quiet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_4: With the engine back, Dewey meant to finish the Ark this time and asked us for parts, a battery and sheet metal.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_5a: With the parts we found, the Ark finally ran. Two tries and one theft, Dewey says, make it a real Kentucky truck.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_5x: The parts ran short again. The engine sits on a stand in the garage, and some nights Dewey polishes it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_1: A voice claiming to be battalion command broke weeks of silence on Whitaker's channel, with codes he half recognized.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_2: Command ordered him to close the checkpoint and burn the refugee camp beside it as an infection risk. He had not answered yet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_3: Casey said the signal was fake and Pike begged him to refuse. We had to choose whose word to back.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_4f: We helped Casey, who traced the 'command' signal to raiders using a stolen military radio. Whitaker was furious.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_4p: We sided with Pike. Whitaker refused the order and sent the camp's people to the church; two soldiers called him a traitor and left.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_4o: Whitaker sealed the checkpoint as ordered. The refugees burned their own shelters and left, and his squad would not meet his eyes.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_4x: The checkpoint was never sealed, and command went silent again.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_5: The noise at the checkpoint drew a horde toward the camp, and Whitaker called for support.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_6a: We cleared the horde and the checkpoint held. Whitaker no longer waits for orders; he calls it 'our county'.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_6f: We cleared the horde and the checkpoint held. With the raiders' radio smashed, Whitaker now trusts Casey's ears over any voice claiming rank.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_6x: The horde broke the checkpoint. Whitaker led what was left north, and his frequency went dead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_1: Privates Cole and Mendez, Whitaker's deserters, had turned up working for Vic's crew.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_2: Whitaker wanted them back for discipline, Vic would not give them up, and Ray was hiding the scared one at his farm. We had to choose.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_3a: Cole came back on his own. Whitaker put him on latrine duty and said nothing more, and the squad noticed.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_3r: We helped Ray. One deserter stayed hidden at his farm, and Whitaker stopped speaking to Ray.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_3v: We backed Vic. Both deserters stayed with him, and now he knows the camp's watch schedule.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_3x: The deserters vanished. Whitaker doubled the watch and sleeps in his boots.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_4: Down to four soldiers, Whitaker asked us for sheet metal, nails and ammunition to fortify the camp before winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_5a: With the materials we sent, the camp was fortified. The four of them hold it, and they trade with civilians at the gate.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_5x: The camp could not be held. Whitaker walked north with the last of his squad.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_1: The Iron Horse, a Louisville gang, said Coalfield was theirs now and Vic's trading post owed them half.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_2: Vic said he needed guns to tell the Iron Horse no.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_3: Showing the ammunition we found, Vic turned the Iron Horse away at the bridge. They promised to come back.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_3x: No ammunition came, so Vic paid them tribute to buy time. The crew muttered that he had gone soft.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_4: The Iron Horse drove the dead ahead of their attack, through our side of the county, and Vic asked us to break the herd.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_5a: We broke the herd, and the Iron Horse broke on Vic's barricades. His trading post is the strongest thing in the south county.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_5x: The herd was never broken. The Iron Horse reached the barricades, and Vic did not run.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_1: Vic called on a different frequency. Dutch ran the crew like a warlord, and three of Vic's old boys wanted him back.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_2: Vic asked us for weapons for the men still loyal to him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_3: With the weapons we found, Vic's boys were armed. He set the night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_3x: No weapons came, and one of the boys talked. Dutch knew something was coming.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_4: Vic meant to take the crew back that night. Hank offered cover, and Whitaker wanted the whole crew arrested. It was up to us.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_5a: Vic was the boss again. Dutch was gone, and the crew was smaller and quieter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_5g: We backed Whitaker. His soldiers raided Coalfield and Dutch was killed. Vic slipped away south and went off the air.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_5x: Dutch found out. Vic went in anyway and did not come back. Only Dutch's threats come over the Coalfield frequency now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_1: In the pack of the hiker Hank had buried, he found a notebook. The man had been walking home to a wife and son.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_2: The hiker's house was on our side of the county, thick with the dead. Hank asked us to clear it so he could see if the family was there.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_3: We cleared the dead. The house was empty, with a note on the door: 'Gone to the March Ridge church.' Hank decided to carry the notebook there himself.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_3x: Nobody got near the house. Hank read the notebook at night and talked about the man as if he had known him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_4: Hank set out to carry a dead man's notebook to his family and asked us for supplies for the trip.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_5a: With the supplies we sent, Hank found the hiker's wife and gave her the notebook. She sends him preserves every month, and he pretends not to care.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_5c: The family was safe at Pike's church. Hank gave them the notebook and stayed for supper, the first in years he had shared with anyone.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_5x: Hank never found the family. The notebook sits on the shelf by his cabin door.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_1: Hank packed to leave the county. One thing remained before he went: taking up his trap lines.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_2: He needed a good knife and rope to take up the traps.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_3: With the knife and rope we sent, the traps came up. Walking the lines one last time, Hank caught himself thinking about staying.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_3x: Half the traps were left in the snow. Hank was angry about it, which meant he cared.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_4: Hank said he would stay one more winter if the cabin had an axe for firewood and enough food stored.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_5a: With the axe and food we sent, Hank stayed. Only one more winter, he says. Everyone knows better.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_5x: Hank left. He left the cabin key under the stone by the door, for us.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_1a: Annie's working the fields beside me. First real harvest since it all fell apart, and I keep stopping just to watch her.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_1b: Lily's helping bring in the harvest, bossing the scarecrow around. First real harvest since the fall.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_1c: Bringing in the harvest alone. More corn and squash than one man could ever eat.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_2: Somebody's watching the farm from the treeline. Boot prints in the corn, and the dogs bark all night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_3: Raiders are herding the dead toward my farm to run me off before the harvest is in. Can you help?
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_4: Fields are safe and the barn's full. I'd like to share it with Pike's church before winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_4x: While the dead kept me inside, they burned half the corn. I saved what I could.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_5: I need sacks and twine to haul the harvest over to the church.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_5x: Half the crop's ash. I'll need canned food to get through the winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_6a: My harvest fed Pike's church too. The preacher and I said grace together over the radio.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_6b: Kept the harvest, but couldn't haul it all. Some of it's rotting in the barn, and it eats at me.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_6c: Thanks to what you sent, the farm will make it through winter. Barely.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_6x: Barn's nearly empty going into winter. I'm rationing everything. Not going to complain.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_1a: The station's busy every night now. People I've never met know my voice.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_1b: I only broadcast at night now, quietly. Fewer people answer, but some still do.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_2: A man calling himself Private Ellis, an Army signals tech, asked to stay at the shack. He knows radios way better than me.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_3: I can't decide if I should trust Ellis. Sergeant Whitaker wants to check him out, and Hank wants to follow him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_4a: Ellis was the real deal! He rebuilt my transmitter and taught me tricks I never knew.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_4g: Whitaker checked him out: a deserter, but harmless. Ellis joined the squad.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_4h: Hank followed Ellis to an Iron Horse camp. He was a spy. Hank ran him off. My hands are still shaking.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_4n: Ellis stayed a few nights, fixed a wire and moved on north. I never found out who he really was.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_4x: Ellis left in the night with half my batteries. I feel so stupid for letting him in.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_5: I want a backup transmitter before winter, so the county never goes quiet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_5x: Without batteries I can only broadcast an hour a night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_6a: I've got a backup transmitter! Whatever winter does, the county will hear me.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_6b: One transmitter, no backup. I keep my fingers crossed every night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_6c: I'm back on the air every night. I don't let strangers in anymore.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_6x: Most nights I stay silent to save the batteries. I hate how quiet it is.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_1a: The clinic runs like a clinic again: a line in the morning, clean sheets, a schedule on the wall.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_1b: I'm the church's nurse now. I keep my kit in the vestry and see patients between prayers.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_1c: I still check every arm at the door. Fewer people come, but nobody has hidden a bite since.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_2: Medicine is running out county-wide. I want to grow herbs. The boy whose leg I set, older now, wants to be my apprentice.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_3: I need garden tools to start the herb beds.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_4: The herb beds are planted: chamomile, feverfew, willow cuttings. Pike's people came to help dig.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_4x: No tools came. The boy and I are drying wild herbs from the riverbank instead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_5: A pack of the dead is drifting through the fields toward the clinic. My apprentice wants to fight. I won't let him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_6a: The herb garden is growing and my apprentice learns fast. Willow bark for pain, chamomile for sleep. Not much, but ours.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_6b: No garden, but my apprentice knows which riverbank weeds bring a fever down. I'm proud of him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_6x: The dead trampled everything, and my apprentice got hurt trying to stop them. He'll heal. I'm not sure I will.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_1a: The church is full of life. Children run between the pews and someone is always cooking.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_1b: Someone else keeps order at the church now. I still lead the prayers, and people still come to me.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_1c: The church is quieter than it was. I look after the few who stayed.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_2: Two refugees, Daniel and Rosa, asked me to marry them. It would be the county's first wedding since the fall.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_3: I'd like a real wedding feast, with candles and something to toast with.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_4: Everyone is invited. Ray promised vegetables, and Casey will broadcast the vows.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_4x: There will be no feast, only vows. Daniel and Rosa say that is enough.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_5: The dead are gathering on the road to the church the day before the wedding.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_6a: Daniel and Rosa were married with candles and a feast. Half the county listened, and I wept again.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_6b: A simple wedding: vows, a borrowed ring, a hymn. Everyone came, and nobody missed the feast.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_6x: We held the wedding in the basement while the dead beat on the doors. A guest was bitten on the way in.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_1a: The Ark runs and everybody wants a ride somewhere. It drinks fuel like you wouldn't believe.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_1b: No Ark, but the garage is busy. Everybody in the county brings me something broken.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_2: Gas is running out across the county. Every pump I know is bone dry.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_3: Found a gas station with a full underground tank. Thing is, it's crawling with the dead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_4: Station's clear and the tank's full. Now I just need a pump and hoses to get it out.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_4x: Couldn't get to the tank. I'm siphoning wrecks one can at a time.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_5: I need hoses and tools to draw the fuel out of that tank.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_5x: Siphoning takes hoses, and I keep wrecking mine.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_6a: Fuel for the whole winter. Half the county runs on gas I pumped, and I like that more than I let on.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_6b: The tank's right there, but I'm bucketing it out. It'll do for now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_6c: Can by can, I scraped together enough for winter. My hands smell like gas all the time.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_6x: No fuel. The garage is cold, and the engines in it are just metal now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_1a: The checkpoint holds. Civilians pass every day, and more of them stop to talk to the soldiers.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_1b: The camp holds with four of us. Civilians trade at the gate, and some of them linger.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_2: Civilians asked me to train them. I refused twice. Then a farm kid died because nobody taught him to hold a rifle.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_3: I am training volunteers. I need practice ammunition.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_4: The volunteers can shoot now. Live drill next, against real dead, and I will watch every one of them.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_4x: Training without ammunition is just shouting. Some quit. A few stayed.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_5: Running a live drill against a real group of the dead. Requesting the players' support.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_6a: The county has a militia: twelve volunteers who can hold a line. I will not say I am proud of them.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_6b: A small militia: five volunteers, green but brave. It is a start.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_6x: A volunteer died in the drill. I disbanded them. I do it all myself again.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_1a: My trading post is the strongest thing in the south county. People come from farther every week.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_1b: The crew's smaller and quieter since Dutch. I'm trying something new: being trusted.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_2: I'm holding a market day in Coalfield, first since the fall. Anyone can come. No robbing. Vic's word.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_3: The stalls need goods. Food, tools, bandages.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_4: Stalls are full. Painted the sign myself. It's crooked.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_4x: The stalls are thin. I'll sell what I've got and talk big about the rest.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_5: A horde's drifting toward Coalfield on market day.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_6a: Market day was a hit. Made it monthly. People shake my hand now. Don't know what to do with that.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_6b: Small market, but nobody got robbed and everybody went home alive. I call that a win.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_6x: The dead broke up the market and a trader died. Nobody came back the next month.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_1a: Autumn in the woods. Lines at dawn, the hiker's notebook by the fire.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_1b: I stayed, and autumn came. Cabin's warm. I stayed for the deer. Let's leave it at that.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_2: Something's springing my traps and taking the catch. Not an animal. Small boot prints. Careful ones.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_3: Going to track it for days. Need supplies for it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_4: Found the thief. A starving young deserter, one of Whitaker's. Have to decide what to do with him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_4x: Never found the thief. The stealing just stopped. I still check for prints every morning.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_6a: The kid lives at the cabin now, learning traps. Talks too much. I let him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_6g: Whitaker took the kid back. Right by the book. I hate the book.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_6r: The kid works Ray's farm now. I visit Sundays. Say it's for the pie.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_6n: Left food at the lean-to and walked off. He's gone now. Hope he made it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_6x: The kid ran off into the cold before anyone could help. Lean-to was empty the next week.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_martha1_1: I took over Ray's farm and his radio. Found his notebook of frequencies too. Keep it by the set.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_nora1_1: I came down from Brandenburg to keep Casey's frequency alive. Her logbook is full of names. I'm learning them one by one.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_sam1_1: I'm running June's clinic now, with her notes and her kit. I'm seventeen. Honestly, I'm terrified.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_esther1_1: There's no preacher at the church now. I keep the kitchen going and the doors open, and I answer the radio.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_lenny1_1: I'm running Dewey's garage now. I know half of what she knew. I talk to her tools when nobody's around.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_kowalski1_1: I am in command of what is left of the squad. Nobody trained me for this. Everyone is watching me. ...Out.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_red1_1: I'm holding the Coalfield crew together since the raid. Fewer fights, more deals.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dutch1_1: Coalfield's mine now. Vic's gone. Everyone on this frequency is going to learn some respect.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_caleb1_1: I came looking for Hank and found his cabin empty. I stayed. My father would've wanted someone to keep the lines.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_1a: Annie worked the fields beside Ray. The first real harvest since the fall was coming in.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_1b: Lily helped Ray bring in the harvest, the first real one since the fall.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_1c: Ray brought in the harvest alone, more corn and squash than one man could eat.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_2: Someone watched Ray's farm from the treeline. There were boot prints in the corn.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_3: Raiders herded the dead toward the farm to drive Ray off before the harvest, and he asked us for help.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_4: We cleared the dead and the fields and barn were saved. Ray wanted to share the harvest with Pike's church.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_4x: The horde stayed, and in the chaos raiders burned half the corn.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_5: Ray asked for sacks and twine to haul the harvest to the church.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_5x: With half his crop gone, Ray asked for canned food to get through winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_6a: With the sacks we sent, the harvest reached the church. Ray and Pike said grace together over the radio.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_6b: No sacks came. Ray kept the harvest but could not haul it, and some of it rotted in the barn.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_6c: With the cans we sent, Ray's farm would just about make it through winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_6x: No cans came. Ray went into winter with a nearly empty barn.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_1a: Casey's station was busy every night; strangers knew her voice.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_1b: Casey broadcast quietly, only at night. Fewer answered, but some still did.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_2: A man calling himself Private Ellis, an Army signals tech, asked to stay at Casey's shack.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_3: Casey could not decide whether to trust Ellis. Whitaker wanted to check him and Hank wanted to follow him. We had to choose.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_4a: Ellis was the real thing. He rebuilt Casey's transmitter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_4g: Whitaker found Ellis was a harmless deserter, and he joined the squad.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_4h: Hank followed Ellis to an Iron Horse camp, exposed him as a spy and ran him off.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_4n: Ellis stayed a few nights and moved on north. Nobody learned who he really was.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_4x: Ellis vanished in the night with half of Casey's batteries.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_5: Casey wanted a backup transmitter before winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_5x: Without her batteries, Casey could broadcast only an hour a night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_6a: With the parts we found, Casey built a backup transmitter. Whatever winter brings, the county will hear her.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_6b: No parts came. Casey would face the winter with a single transmitter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_6c: With the batteries we sent, Casey is back on the air every night. She lets no strangers in now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_6x: No batteries came, and Casey spends most nights silent.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc3_1a: June's clinic ran like a clinic again, with a line every morning.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc3_1b: June worked as the church's nurse, seeing patients between prayers.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc3_1c: June still checked every arm at the clinic door.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc3_2: With medicine running out, June decided to grow herbs, and the boy whose leg she had set offered to be her apprentice.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc3_3: June asked for garden tools to start the herb beds.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc3_4: With the tools we sent, the herb beds went in, and Pike's people came to help dig.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc3_4x: No tools came, so June and the boy dried wild herbs from the riverbank.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc3_5: A pack of the dead drifted through the fields toward the clinic, and June asked for help.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc3_6a: We cleared the dead. The herb garden grows, and the apprentice learns fast.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc3_6b: We cleared the dead. There was no garden, but the apprentice learned which weeds bring a fever down.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc3_6x: The dead stayed. They trampled everything, and the apprentice was hurt trying to stop them.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike3_1a: Pike's church was full of life.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike3_1b: Someone else kept order at the church, but people still came to Pike.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike3_1c: The church had grown quiet, and Pike looked after the few who stayed.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike3_2: Two refugees, Daniel and Rosa, wanted to marry: the county's first wedding since the fall.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike3_3: Pike asked for candles, food and something to toast with for the feast.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike3_4: With what we sent, the feast was ready, and the whole county was invited.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike3_4x: There was no feast. Daniel and Rosa said vows were enough.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike3_5: The day before the wedding, the dead gathered on the road to the church.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike3_6a: We cleared the road. They were married by candlelight with a feast, and half the county listened.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike3_6b: We cleared the road. It was a simple wedding, but everyone came.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike3_6x: The road stayed blocked. They married in the basement, and a guest was bitten on the way in.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_1a: The Ark ran, and drank fuel like nothing else.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_1b: There was no Ark, but Dewey's garage was always busy.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_2: Gasoline was running out across the county.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_3: Dewey found a gas station with a full underground tank, thick with the dead, and asked us to clear it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_4: We cleared the station. Now Dewey needed gear to draw the fuel up.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_4x: The station stayed overrun. Dewey siphoned wrecks one can at a time.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_5: Dewey asked for hoses and tools.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_5x: Dewey asked for hoses to replace the ones she kept ruining.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_6a: With the hoses we sent, the tank was tapped. Half the county runs on fuel Dewey pumped.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_6b: No hoses came. Dewey bucketed the fuel out.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_6c: With the hoses we sent, Dewey scraped together the winter's fuel can by can.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_6x: No fuel came, and the garage went cold.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard3_1a: The checkpoint held, and passing civilians stopped to talk to the soldiers.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard3_1b: Civilians traded at the gate of the camp the four soldiers held.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard3_2: Civilians asked for training. Whitaker refused until a farm kid died for not knowing how to hold a rifle.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard3_3: Whitaker asked for practice ammunition for his volunteers.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard3_4: With the ammunition we sent, the volunteers learned to shoot.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard3_4x: No ammunition came, and some volunteers quit.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard3_5: Whitaker ran a live drill against a real group of the dead and called us in.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard3_6a: The drill went well with us there. The county had a militia.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard3_6b: The drill went well. A small militia, but a start.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard3_6x: A volunteer died in the drill, and Whitaker disbanded them.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_1a: Vic's trading post was the strongest thing in the south county.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_1b: Since Dutch, Vic's crew had grown smaller and quieter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_2: Vic decided to hold Coalfield's first market day. Anyone could come; no robbing.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_3: Vic asked for goods to fill the stalls.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_4: With the goods we sent, the stalls were full.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_4x: No goods came, and the stalls were thin.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_5: On market day a horde drifted toward Coalfield.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_6a: We cleared the horde. Market day was a hit and became monthly.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_6b: We cleared the horde. A small market, but everyone got home safe.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_6x: The horde broke up the market, and a trader died.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_1a: Autumn came to the woods. Hank checked his lines every dawn.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_1b: Autumn came for Hank, who had stayed.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_2: Something sprang Hank's traps and stole the catch, leaving small boot prints.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_3: Hank asked for supplies to track the thief for days.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_4: With the supplies we sent, Hank found the thief: a starving young deserter. We had to decide what to do with him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_4x: The thief was never found, and the stealing stopped on its own.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_6a: The boy lives at Hank's cabin now, learning traps.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_6g: Whitaker took the boy back. Hank hated the book that said so.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_6r: The boy became Ray's farm hand, and Hank visits on Sundays.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_6n: Hank left food and walked away. The boy was gone.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_6x: The boy ran off into the cold before anyone could help.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_martha1_1: Ray's neighbor Martha Cole took over his farm and his radio.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_nora1_1: Nora Bell, a radio operator from Brandenburg, took over Casey's frequency.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_sam1_1: Sam, June's seventeen-year-old apprentice, took over the clinic.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_esther1_1: Esther Gray, who ran the church kitchen, began answering the radio.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_lenny1_1: Lenny Austin, Dewey's apprentice, took over the garage.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_kowalski1_1: Corporal Kowalski took command of what was left of the squad.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_red1_1: Red, who had stayed with the crew, held Coalfield together.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_caleb1_1: Earl's son, Caleb Tate, took over Hank's cabin.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_ellis: A man calling himself Private Ellis has been staying at Casey's shack. Casey wants to trust him, Whitaker wants to check him, and Hank wants to follow him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_ellis_casey: Asks for food and blankets to keep her guest properly.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_ellis_guard: Will pick Ellis up and check his story if given 5.56 ammunition.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_ellis_hunter: Will follow Ellis to see where he really goes if given rifle ammunition.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_thief: The thief raiding Hank's traps is a starving young deserter from Whitaker's squad. Hank could take him in, Whitaker wants him back, and Ray could use a farm hand.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_thief_hunter: Asks for food and blankets so he can take the boy in.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_thief_guard: Will send the squad to collect their deserter if given 5.56 ammunition.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_thief_ray: Asks for canned food to feed the boy as a farm hand.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_doc_family_appr: Apprentice - the boy whose leg she set
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_guard_family_mi: The squad and a twelve-strong civilian militia
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_hunter_family_a: A young deserter living at the cabin, learning traps
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_martha_home: Ray Mercer's farmhouse outside West Point
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_martha_bio: The widow from the farm next to Ray's, who promised to watch his farm. Blunt, generous, and allergic to sentiment.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_nora_bio: A radio operator from Brandenburg who used to listen to Casey. Calm, wry, organized. Learning the county from Casey's logbook.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_sam_family: Lost his family, grew up at the clinic
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_sam_bio: The boy whose broken leg June set, now her seventeen-year-old apprentice, running the clinic with her notes. Earnest, scared, learning fast.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_esther_family: The church folk are her family
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_esther_job: Ran the church kitchen and storeroom
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_esther_bio: The woman who ran the church kitchen and storeroom. She doesn't preach; she keeps the place running. Practical, warm, no patience for nonsense.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_lenny_bio: A young man Dewey was teaching. Eager, clumsy, and he worshipped Dewey.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_kowalski_bio: The last corporal of Whitaker's squad, suddenly in command. Tries to sound like Whitaker and fails.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_red_bio: A sharp-tongued woman who stayed with the crew after the raid. Tired of fighting; wants more deals and fewer fights.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_dutch_bio: Vic's former second, now running the Coalfield crew like a warlord. Menacing, greedy, enjoys threats.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_caleb_family: His father Earl was Hank's hunting partner
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_caleb_home: The cabin in the Ekron woods
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_caleb_bio: Son of Hank's late hunting partner Earl. Came looking for Hank and took over the empty cabin. Quiet like Hank, gentler.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Voice_Line: A new voice has taken over this frequency: %1
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray4_1a: Winter came hard. I've got a cough that won't quit, and Annie keeps feeling my forehead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray4_1b: Winter came hard. Got a cough that won't quit, and Lily keeps bringing me tea she made all wrong.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray4_1c: Winter came hard. Got a cough that won't quit, and nobody out here to fuss over it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray4_2a: This is Annie on Dad's radio. He collapsed in the barn with a fever. He can't get up.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray4_2b: This is Lily. Mister Ray fell down. He's really hot and he won't wake up properly. What do I do?
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray4_3: Cough... it's pneumonia. I need antibiotics before it gets worse... Please.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray4_4: The fever broke. Weak as a kitten, but alive. The house is freezing, though.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray4_4x: The fever broke on its own, slowly. I'm alive, but I'll meet the spring a frailer man.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray4_5: I need firewood and blankets to keep the house warm while I get my strength back.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray4_6a: Warm house, full woodpile, and I'm on my feet again. Never been so glad to see snow.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray4_6b: Made it through burning old furniture. Thin as a rail, but on my feet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey4_1a: Winter on the air. On the worst nights I switch to the backup. The county never goes quiet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey4_1b: Winter on the air. My one transmitter coughs in the cold. I nurse it like a sick puppy.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey4_2: The blizzard knocked the antenna mast down. Nobody can hear me, and the dead won't let me near the mast.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey4_3: The dead are drifting around the fallen mast in the snow. Can you help?
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey4_4: The mast is clear! I need wire and screws to raise it before the next storm.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey4_4x: The mast stayed down for a month. The county got through the worst of winter without my voice, and everyone felt it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey4_6a: The mast is up, taller and stronger! I came back on the air mid-blizzard and people cheered.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey4_6b: The mast is up again, held with tape and prayers. It sways, but it works.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc4_1a: Winter at the clinic: frostbite, coughs, and my apprentice tending the herb tea kettle all day.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc4_1b: Winter at the clinic. My apprentice still limps from the fall, so I'm doing it all alone again.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc4_2: Rosa, the bride from Pike's church, is pregnant, and the baby is coming early, in the dead of winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc4_3: I need clean dressings and disinfectant for a birth.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc4_4: My bag is packed for the birth. The problem is the road to the church. It's full of the dead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc4_4x: I'll have to make do with boiled rags. And the road to the church is full of the dead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc4_5: Rosa's labor has started and the road to the church is full of the dead. Please help.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc4_6a: A girl, small and loud, born at dawn in Pike's church. They named her Hope. The whole county heard her cry on the radio.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc4_6b: The baby came fast, with nothing but boiled rags. Mother and girl are both alive. I didn't sleep for two days.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc4_6x: I got there too late. The baby lived. Rosa didn't. I held the girl and couldn't say anything for a long time.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike4_1a: Winter in the church. Daniel and Rosa's wedding still makes people smile, and the stove burns day and night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike4_1b: Winter in the church. People are cold and frightened since the wedding night, and the stores are thin.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike4_2: Food kept disappearing from the storeroom. Last night I caught the thief: a starving twelve-year-old with nobody to look after him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike4_3: The congregation is split about the boy: forgive him, punish him, or send him away.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike4_4a: I forgave the boy and gave him chores. He works harder than anyone and sleeps by the stove like a cat.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike4_4g: Whitaker's soldiers took the boy to work at the camp. No more theft since. No joy either.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike4_4r: The boy went to work for Vic in Coalfield. He's fed. I pray he doesn't learn the wrong things.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike4_4n: Nobody could agree, so I simply kept feeding him. The arguing died down on its own.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike4_4x: The boy ran off into the snow before anything was decided. I searched for two days.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike4_5: The storeroom has to last until spring, and it won't without help.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike4_6a: The storeroom will last until spring. Nobody has to steal anymore, and I made sure everyone knows it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike4_6b: Half rations until spring. I eat last and least, and people have noticed.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey4_1a: Winter, and I've got fuel. Half the county calls me when their engine won't start in the cold.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey4_1b: Winter, and barely any fuel. I saved a few cans for a real emergency.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey4_2: A farm family's snowed in east of Echo Creek with a sick kid. I'm the only one with a truck that can get there.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey4_3: The only road to that farm is thick with the dead. Clear it for me.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey4_4: Got the family out! The kid's with June now. The truck took a beating on the ice, though.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey4_4x: I took the road anyway. The truck slid off the ice and pinned my leg. The family's still out there and I can't work.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey4_5: The rescue run wrecked the suspension. I need parts before the next emergency.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey4_5x: My leg's broken. I need a splint and painkillers, and somebody to bring them.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey4_6a: Truck's fixed, and I'm the county's winter rescue now. Nobody voted. I just go when they call.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey4_6b: The truck limps. One more run like that and it's done.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey4_6c: Leg's splinted and healing. Someone else got that family out in the end. I'm furious it wasn't me.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey4_6x: My leg healed wrong. I walk with a cane now. Never found out what happened to that family.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard4_1a: Winter at the checkpoint. The militia stands watch in the snow with the soldiers. It works.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard4_1b: Winter at the camp. Fewer hands than I'd like, and the cold gets into everything.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard4_2: A real military broadcast came through: all units regroup at Fort Knox. Real codes this time. The squad wants to go.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard4_3: I have to decide: go to Fort Knox with the squad, or stay with the people who depend on us.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard4_4l: I am going to Fort Knox. Orders are orders. I am leaving Kowalski the radio and a list of names. ...Take care.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard4_4c: Casey checked the broadcast: real, but weeks old. Knox went quiet after it. I am staying. I do not know how I feel.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard4_4s: I stayed. The squad grumbled, then stayed with me. I told them the county is the mission now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard4_5: Staying means getting through winter on what we have. We are short on ammunition.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard4_6a: We held through the winter. The squad calls the county home now. So, quietly, do I.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard4_6b: We held, barely, counting every round. Staying was right. I keep telling myself that.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats4_1a: Winter market days are smaller, but people still come. Stove's hot, prices are fair. Mostly.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats4_1b: Winter in Coalfield. Since the market went bad, I mostly sit by the stove counting what's left.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats4_2: Someone saw my little brother Tony among the dead near you. He went missing the first week. Never told anyone I had a brother.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats4_3: My brother Tony's out there, turned. I can't do it. I'm asking anyway.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats4_4: You put Tony to rest and brought back his jacket. Didn't say thanks. Couldn't say anything.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats4_4x: Tony's still out there. I stopped running the market. I drink at night and don't answer the radio much.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats4_5: I want to bury Tony's jacket proper, in Coalfield, with a marker. Need tools to break the frozen ground.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats4_6a: Tony has a marker now. Pike came to say the words and I let him. And I finally said thanks to you.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats4_6b: Kept the jacket by the stove instead. Spring, maybe, when the ground thaws.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter4_1a: Winter at the cabin with the kid. He chops wood badly and talks nonstop. I've stopped minding.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter4_1b: Winter at the cabin, alone. Snow's deep and the lines are quiet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter4_2: Casey read a message on the air. Earl's boy, Caleb, is alive and looking for me near Rosewood.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter4_3: The snow road toward Rosewood is full of the dead. I'm going to find Earl's boy.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter4_4: Found Caleb half frozen in a farmhouse near Rosewood. He's got Earl's eyes. He's at the cabin now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter4_4x: Never found Caleb. Left a note with Casey to read every week. Just in case.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter4_5: One more mouth at the cabin this winter. Need food stored and warm blankets.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter4_6a: Caleb's staying for good. He fixes things and listens more than he talks. Earl would've liked that.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter4_6b: Lean winter at the cabin. Caleb splits his rations with me. I won't admit I'm glad he's here.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray4_1a: A hard winter came. Ray's cough would not quit, and Annie stayed close.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray4_1b: A hard winter came. Ray's cough would not quit, and Lily brought him badly made tea.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray4_1c: A hard winter came, and Ray coughed through it alone.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray4_2a: One day Annie's voice came over Ray's radio: he had collapsed with a fever.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray4_2b: One day Lily's voice came over Ray's radio: Mister Ray had fallen down and would not wake properly.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray4_3: It was pneumonia. Wheezing, Ray asked us for antibiotics.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray4_4: The antibiotics we found broke the fever, but the farmhouse was freezing.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray4_4x: No medicine reached him. The fever broke slowly on its own, and Ray came out of it much frailer.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray4_5: Ray asked for firewood and blankets while he got his strength back.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray4_6a: With the firewood and blankets we sent, the house warmed up and Ray got back on his feet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray4_6b: No firewood came. Ray burned old furniture to get through.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey4_1a: Through the winter nights Casey kept broadcasting on the backup transmitter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey4_1b: Casey nursed her one coughing transmitter through the winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey4_2: A blizzard brought down Casey's antenna mast.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey4_3: The dead gathered around the fallen mast, and Casey asked us to clear them.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey4_4: We cleared the dead. Casey asked for wire and screws to raise the mast.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey4_4x: The mast stayed surrounded. The county went a month of winter without Casey's voice.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey4_6a: With what we sent, the mast went up taller and stronger, and people cheered when she came back on air in a blizzard.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey4_6b: No materials came. The mast sways, held up with tape.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc4_1a: Winter at the clinic was busy with frostbite and coughs; the apprentice kept the herb tea going.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc4_1b: With her apprentice still limping, June ran the winter clinic alone.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc4_2: Rosa, the bride from Pike's church, was going into early labor in the dead of winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc4_3: June asked for dressings and disinfectant for the birth.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc4_4: With what we sent, her birth bag was ready. The road to the church was the problem.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc4_4x: No supplies came. June would make do with boiled rags.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc4_5: Rosa's labor began, and the road to the church was choked with the dead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc4_6a: We opened the road. A girl named Hope was born at dawn, and the whole county heard her cry.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc4_6b: We opened the road. There were only boiled rags, but mother and baby both lived.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc4_6x: The road stayed shut. June arrived too late; the baby lived, but Rosa died.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike4_1a: Winter in the church was warm with the memory of the wedding.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike4_1b: Winter in the church was cold and frightened.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike4_2: Food kept vanishing from the storeroom. The thief was a twelve-year-old with nobody to care for him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike4_3: The congregation was split, and it fell to us to decide.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike4_4a: We helped Pike. The boy was forgiven and works at the church now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike4_4g: We backed Whitaker. The boy was put to work at the camp.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike4_4r: We took Vic's offer. The boy went to work in Coalfield.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike4_4n: Nothing was decided, and Pike simply kept feeding the boy.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike4_4x: Before anything was decided, the boy ran off into the snow.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike4_5: Pike asked for food to last the church until spring.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike4_6a: With the food we sent, the storeroom will last until spring.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike4_6b: No food came. The church lives on half rations until spring.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey4_1a: When winter came, everyone called Dewey when their engines would not start.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey4_1b: With barely any fuel, Dewey saved a few cans for emergencies.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey4_2: A family with a sick child was snowed in east of Echo Creek, and only Dewey had a truck that could reach them.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey4_3: The road to that farm was thick with the dead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey4_4: We cleared the road, and Dewey got the family out.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey4_4x: The road was not cleared. Dewey went anyway, and her leg was pinned under the truck.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey4_5: The truck, wrecked by the rescue, needed parts.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey4_5x: With a broken leg, Dewey asked for a splint and painkillers.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey4_6a: With the parts we sent, the truck was fixed, and Dewey became the county's winter rescue.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey4_6b: No parts came. The truck limps along.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey4_6c: With the splint we sent, Dewey's leg is healing. Someone else rescued the family in the end.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey4_6x: No splint came. Her leg healed wrong, and Dewey walks with a cane.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard4_1a: Through the winter, the militia stood watch at the checkpoint with the soldiers.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard4_1b: The cold seeped into the short-handed camp.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard4_2: A real military broadcast ordered all units to Fort Knox, and the squad wanted to go.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard4_3: Whitaker had to choose between leaving and staying, and it was our call.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard4_4l: Whitaker led the squad north to Fort Knox, leaving Kowalski the radio and a list of names.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard4_4c: Casey checked the broadcast: real, but weeks old. Whitaker stayed.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard4_4s: We sided with Pike, and Whitaker and his squad stayed in the county.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard4_5: Having stayed, the squad was short on ammunition for the winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard4_6a: With the ammunition we sent, they held through the winter. The squad calls the county home now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard4_6b: No ammunition came. The squad held, barely, counting every round.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats4_1a: Even in winter, Vic's market still opened, if smaller.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats4_1b: After the market failed, Vic sat by the stove counting what was left.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats4_2: Vic's little brother Tony was seen among the dead near us. It was the first time Vic ever mentioned a brother.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats4_3: Vic could not do it himself and asked us to put Tony to rest.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats4_4: We put Tony to rest and brought back his jacket. Vic could not say a word.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats4_4x: Tony still walks out there. Vic closed the market and drinks at night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats4_5: Vic asked for tools to bury Tony's jacket under a marker.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats4_6a: With the tools we sent, Tony got a marker. Pike said the words, and Vic finally thanked us.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats4_6b: No tools came. The jacket waits by the stove for spring.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter4_1a: Hank spent the winter at the cabin with the kid.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter4_1b: Hank spent the winter alone in the deep snow.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter4_2: Casey's broadcast carried word that Earl's son Caleb was alive and looking for Hank.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter4_3: The snow road toward Rosewood was full of the dead, and Hank asked us to clear the way.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter4_4: We cleared the way. Hank found Caleb half frozen and brought him to the cabin.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter4_4x: The road stayed blocked and Caleb was not found. Hank asked Casey to read a note every week.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter4_5: With another mouth at the cabin, Hank needed food and blankets.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter4_6a: With the food and blankets we sent, they wintered well, and Caleb decided to stay for good.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter4_6b: No food came. Caleb split his rations, and they got through a lean winter together.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_martha1_2: Ray's notebook has a page for every neighbor he traded with. Half of them still need something.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_martha1_3: The farm needs work before next season, and I can't do it alone at my age. Find me some tools.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_martha1_4: The farm's running. Found a letter Ray never sent, to Annie. I put it somewhere safe.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_martha1_4x: The farm limps along. Found a letter Ray never sent, to Annie. Read it twice.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_martha1_5: Raiders figured out Ray's gone. They're herding the dead at the farm to test the new owner.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_martha1_6a: The farm held. I put Ray's notebook back by the radio and wrote my name under his.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_martha1_6b: They took the chickens and I took a beating. The farm's still mine. Barely.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_nora1_2: Casey's logbook has forty names. I'm calling them one by one to say the frequency is still alive.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_nora1_3: Casey's transmitter is older than I am. I need parts to keep it running.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_nora1_4: The transmitter hums. Someone on Casey's list asked if Casey's all right. I didn't know what to say.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_nora1_4x: The transmitter crackles and dies every few hours. People are starting to think the frequency is dead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_nora1_5: I want to know what happened to Casey. Her last log mentions a house the dead have surrounded since.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_nora1_6a: I found Casey's last note in that house: 'Keep it on the air.' I read it on the evening broadcast. I'm staying.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_nora1_6b: I never reached that house. I keep the frequency alive anyway, for whoever Casey was talking to.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_sam1_2: June's notes are all shorthand. I can barely read them. I study them every night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_sam1_3: A man came in with a gash only June ever closed. I need a suture kit. And the nerve.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_sam1_4: My first stitches. Crooked, but they held. I threw up after, and then I felt really proud.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_sam1_4x: I closed it with tape and luck. It got infected. He'll live, they say. I still can't sleep.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_sam1_5: Everything June kept stocked is running out.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_sam1_6a: The clinic's stocked and people trust me now. I still talk to June's notes. They still help.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_sam1_6b: The shelves are thin and some people go to Pike's church instead. I keep the door open anyway.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_esther1_2: Everyone keeps asking me to preach. I tell them I cook, I don't preach. They keep asking.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_esther1_3: The kitchen is the heart of this church, and it's nearly empty.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_esther1_4: The kitchen is full. I found the preacher's last sermon in his coat. Unfinished.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_esther1_4x: Thin soup again. I found the preacher's last sermon in his coat. Unfinished.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_esther1_5: I want to read his last sermon to everyone on Sunday. I'd like candles for it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_esther1_6a: I read his sermon by candlelight and finished it in my own words. Nobody asks me to preach anymore. They don't need to.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_esther1_6b: I read the sermon in the dark. It was enough. It had to be.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_lenny1_2: Dewey's tools are all labeled in her handwriting. I haven't moved a single one.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_lenny1_3: Someone's truck died on the road and they called the garage. I need parts and I can't mess this up.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_lenny1_4: It started! I laughed out loud and then cried a little. Dewey should've seen it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_lenny1_4x: Couldn't fix it. They towed it off cursing. I sat in Dewey's chair for an hour.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_lenny1_5: I want to finish what Dewey started. Whatever's left under the tarp in the back.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_lenny1_6a: It runs! I painted 'DEWEY' on the side. People honk when they drive past the garage.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_lenny1_6b: Still under the tarp. Someday. I check the battery every week.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_kowalski1_2: Sergeant Whitaker's list of people to look after is taped above the radio. I am trying to keep every name on it alive.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_kowalski1_3: Ammunition is low. The soldiers are watching to see if I... if I can handle it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_kowalski1_4: We have ammunition and a little respect. I practiced the sergeant's voice in the mirror. It did not help.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_kowalski1_4x: One soldier walked off, saying I am no Whitaker. I am not. I am still here.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_kowalski1_5: A group of the dead is coming at the camp. My first fight in command. Requesting support.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_kowalski1_6a: We held the line in my first fight. Nobody calls me 'kid' anymore. I crossed one name off the worry list.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_kowalski1_6b: I lost two soldiers in my first fight in command. I still keep the list. It is shorter now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_red1_2: The crew's half what it was. I want to trade with everyone, even people Vic hated.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_red1_3: To trade, you need something to sell.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_red1_4: Made my first honest trade. Felt strange. Good strange.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_red1_4x: Nothing to trade, so the crew wants to raid again. I'm holding them back with words.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_red1_5: Outside raiders think we're weak without Vic. They're driving the dead at Coalfield.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_red1_6a: Coalfield held, and people know we trade now instead of robbing. I sleep better than I have in years.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_red1_6b: Coalfield got hit hard. Half the crew wants to go back to raiding. I'm not sure I can stop them.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dutch1_2: Everyone on this frequency, listen up. Coalfield takes a toll now. Pay it, or else.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dutch1_3: You want the roads near Coalfield, you pay the toll. No exceptions.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dutch1_4: You paid. I'm almost disappointed. Almost.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dutch1_5: A horde's coming at Coalfield. ...For once I need hands, not tolls.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dutch1_6a: You saved Coalfield. I hate owing anyone. No toll for you. Only you.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dutch1_6b: Coalfield got overrun and I lost half my men. That's on you. I'll say so on every frequency.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_caleb1_2: Hank's trap lines are overgrown. I'm walking them with his map, slowly.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_caleb1_3: I need proper tools to reset Hank's lines.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_caleb1_4: The lines are set. The first catch felt like my father patting my back.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_caleb1_4x: Half the lines are reset. The rest will have to wait.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_caleb1_5: Something big has been at the smokehouse. I think it's a bear, like the one Hank wrote about.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_caleb1_6a: I got the bear, like Hank did once. Hung its claw by the door, next to Hank's hat.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_caleb1_6b: The bear cleaned out the smokehouse. I'm rebuilding it with a better lock.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_martha1_2: Martha worked through the neighbors in Ray's notebook one by one.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_martha1_3: Martha asked for tools to keep the farm running.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_martha1_4: With the tools we sent, the farm ran. Martha found a letter Ray never sent to Annie.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_martha1_4x: No tools came, and the farm barely got by. Martha found Ray's unsent letter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_martha1_5: Raiders herded the dead at the farm to test its new owner.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_martha1_6a: We cleared the dead. Martha wrote her name under Ray's in the notebook.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_martha1_6b: The dead stayed. The raiders took the chickens, but the farm stayed Martha's.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_nora1_2: Nora called the people in Casey's logbook one by one.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_nora1_3: Nora asked for parts to keep the old transmitter alive.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_nora1_4: With the parts we sent, the transmitter came back to life.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_nora1_4x: No parts came, and the transmitter kept dying.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_nora1_5: Nora wanted to search the house from Casey's last log, and the dead surrounded it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_nora1_6a: We cleared the way. Nora found Casey's note, 'Keep it on the air,' and stayed.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_nora1_6b: The house was never reached. Nora kept the frequency alive anyway.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_sam1_2: Every night Sam studied from June's notes.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_sam1_3: A wound only June had ever closed came in, and Sam asked for a suture kit.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_sam1_4: With the kit we sent, Sam did his first stitches. Crooked, but they held.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_sam1_4x: No kit came. Sam closed the wound with tape, and it got infected.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_sam1_5: The clinic was running out of supplies.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_sam1_6a: With what we sent, the clinic was stocked and people came to trust Sam.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_sam1_6b: Nothing came. Sam keeps the door open in front of empty shelves.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_esther1_2: People asked Esther to preach; she kept to the kitchen.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_esther1_3: With the church kitchen nearly empty, Esther asked for food.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_esther1_4: With the food we sent, the kitchen filled. Esther found the preacher's unfinished sermon.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_esther1_4x: No food came. Esther found the preacher's unfinished sermon.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_esther1_5: Esther asked for candles to read that sermon by.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_esther1_6a: By the candles we sent, Esther read the sermon and finished it in her own words.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_esther1_6b: No candles came. Esther read the sermon in the dark.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_lenny1_2: Lenny did not move a single one of Dewey's tools.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_lenny1_3: Lenny asked for parts to fix a stranded truck.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_lenny1_4: With the parts we sent, the truck started. Lenny laughed, then cried a little.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_lenny1_4x: No parts came, and the truck was towed away.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_lenny1_5: Lenny wanted to finish what Dewey had left under the tarp.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_lenny1_6a: With the parts we sent, it ran. Lenny painted 'DEWEY' on the side.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_lenny1_6b: No parts came. It is still under the tarp.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_kowalski1_2: Kowalski taped Whitaker's list of names above the radio.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_kowalski1_3: Short on ammunition, Kowalski asked for some.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_kowalski1_4: With the ammunition we sent, the squad began to trust Kowalski a little.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_kowalski1_4x: No ammunition came, and one soldier walked off.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_kowalski1_5: A group of the dead came at the camp: Kowalski's first fight in command.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_kowalski1_6a: With us there, the line held. Nobody calls him 'kid' anymore.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_kowalski1_6b: The line broke, and two soldiers were lost.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_red1_2: Red set out to trade with anyone, with a crew half its old size.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_red1_3: Red asked for goods to sell.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_red1_4: With the goods we sent, Red made her first honest trade.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_red1_4x: No goods came, and the crew wanted to raid again.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_red1_5: Outside raiders drove the dead at Coalfield.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_red1_6a: We held them off. Coalfield is known now as a place that trades.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_red1_6b: Coalfield was hit hard, and half the crew wants to raid again.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dutch1_2: Dutch announced a Coalfield toll on every frequency.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dutch1_3: Dutch demanded the toll from us.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dutch1_4x: We refused the toll. Dutch said he would remember.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dutch1_5: When a horde came at Coalfield, Dutch asked for help for the first time.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dutch1_6a: We saved Coalfield. Dutch dropped the toll, for us alone.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dutch1_6b: Coalfield was overrun, and Dutch blames us on every frequency.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_caleb1_2: Caleb walked Hank's overgrown lines with his map.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_caleb1_3: Caleb asked for tools to reset the traps.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_caleb1_4: With the tools we sent, the lines were set and the first catch came in.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_caleb1_4x: No tools came, and only half the lines were set.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_caleb1_5: When a bear raided the smokehouse, Caleb asked for rifle rounds.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_caleb1_6a: With the rounds we sent, Caleb got the bear. Its claw hangs next to Hank's hat.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_caleb1_6b: No rounds came. The bear cleaned out the smokehouse and left.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_pantry: A starving twelve-year-old has been stealing from Pike's church storeroom. Pike wants to forgive him, Whitaker wants him put to work under discipline at the camp, and Vic offers to take him on in Coalfield.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_pantry_pike: Asks for food to replace what the boy took, so he can forgive him and keep him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_pantry_guard: Will take the boy to work at the camp for a box of 9mm rounds.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_pantry_rats: Will take the boy on as a hand in Coalfield for a bottle of whiskey.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_knox: A real order to regroup at Fort Knox came through. Whitaker's squad wants to go north, Pike begs them to stay the winter, and Casey offers to check whether the order is still current.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_knox_guard: Asks for ammunition and food for the march north.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_knox_pike: Asks for food and blankets so the squad can winter in the county.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_knox_casey: Will listen for Fort Knox and check the order if given batteries.

IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_martha_q_declined_: Can't do it? Fine. I'll ask around.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_martha_q_ignored_1: No answer, so I let it go.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_martha_q_thanks_1: Thanks. I see why Ray talked about you.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_martha_q_failed_1: Didn't work out. Well. Next time.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_martha_refuse_1: Not yet. I don't know you well enough.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_martha_offline_rep: Radio's acting up. Call again later.

IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_martha_chat_mornin: Sun's up. Fed the chickens, now I'm calling.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_martha_chat_evenin: Day's done. Lock your doors tight.

IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_nora_q_thanks_1: Thank you, really. Casey would have been grateful too.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_nora_q_failed_1: Didn't work this time. I'll note it in the log.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_nora_request_1: I have a favor to ask. I need %1.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_nora_offer_1: Let's do this. It's a fair trade.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_nora_refuse_1: Not yet. We need to know each other better.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_nora_offline_reply: Signal's weak. Call me again in a bit.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_nora_chat_checkin_: Your names were in Casey's log. I wanted to say hello.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_nora_chat_morning_: Good morning. Looks like clear weather today.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_sam_q_declined_1: Oh, okay... It's fine. I'll manage somehow.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_sam_q_ignored_1: No answer, so... I'll find another way.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_sam_q_thanks_1: Thank you. June would have thanked you like this too.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_sam_q_failed_1: It didn't work... I should've done better.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_sam_request_1: Um... I need a favor. I need %1.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_sam_offer_1: I can give you this. Is that okay?
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_sam_refuse_1: Sorry, I can't give that yet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_sam_offline_reply_: The radio's acting weird. Try again later?
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_sam_chat_checkin_1: You're not hurt, right? Just checking.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_sam_chat_checkin_2: Three patients today. All fine. I just wanted to tell someone.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_sam_chat_morning_1: Good morning. Don't forget to wash your hands!
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_sam_chat_evening_1: Closing up the clinic. Everyone made it through today.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_esther_q_accepted_: Thank you. The Lord will know.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_esther_q_declined_: That's all right. There will be another way.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_esther_q_ignored_1: No word, so I'll let it pass.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_esther_q_thanks_1: Thank you so much. I'll put your names in tonight's prayers.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_esther_q_failed_1: It didn't work out. Thank you for trying all the same.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_esther_request_1: Just one favor. I could use %1.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_esther_offer_1: I can give you this. It isn't much.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_esther_refuse_1: Not just yet. Let's get to know each other a little more.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_esther_offline_rep: I can barely hear you. Call again later, dear.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_esther_chat_checki: Have you eaten? That's what matters most.
The soup came out well today. I wish I could give you a bowl.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_esther_chat_mornin: Good morning. Start the day with something warm.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_esther_chat_evenin: Evening now. Lock the doors and sleep well.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_lenny_q_declined_1: Oh... okay. I'll figure something out.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_lenny_q_ignored_1: No answer. I'll let it go.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_lenny_q_thanks_1: Thanks! I know what Dewey would've said: 'Not bad.'
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_lenny_q_failed_1: Damn, didn't work. Next time for sure.

IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_lenny_offer_1: How about this? I fixed it up myself.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_lenny_refuse_1: Not yet... Dewey said to be picky about customers.

Saved an engine today! Had to brag to someone.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_lenny_chat_morning: Morning! Warm the engine up before you start it in the cold.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_lenny_chat_evening: Closing the garage. Covered in grease again.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_kowalski_q_decline: Understood. We will find another way.

IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_kowalski_offer_1: I can release this. It is within regulations.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_kowalski_chat_chec: Checking the names on the list. You are on it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_kowalski_chat_morn: Morning check. Patrol route clear today.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_red_q_thanks_1: Thanks. I mean it. Rare around here.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_red_q_failed_1: Didn't work. Let's do better next deal.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_red_request_1: One favor. Can you find me %1?
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_red_offer_1: Take this. Fair price, honestly priced.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_red_chat_checkin_2: Two trades today. Nobody got hurt. Imagine that.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_dutch_q_failed_1: Failed, huh. You'll pay for that.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_dutch_refuse_1: Get lost. Not selling to you.

Coalfield's mine. Everyone knows that, right?

IGUI_StoryEngine_Line_dutch_chat_evening: Night. Watch the roads after dark. I mean it.
